events.stem:
Which one of the following statements about electrochemical cells and corrosion is NOT correct?
(A) In standard cell notation, a single vertical line represents the salt bridge.
(B) Zinc or magnesium blocks protect a steel hull because they are oxidised in preference to iron.
(C) A fuel cell converts the energy of a fuel's oxidation directly into electrical energy while the reactants are fed in continuously.
(D) The calomel electrode is a metal–insoluble salt electrode.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Analyze each statement.
(A) In standard cell notation, a single vertical line represents the salt bridge. Standard notation uses a single vertical line (|) to separate electrodes and a double vertical line (||) for the salt bridge. Thus a single vertical line does NOT represent the salt bridge; it separates the two half-cells. Hence (A) is incorrect.
(B) Zinc or magnesium blocks protect a steel hull because they are oxidised in preference to iron. This describes cathodic protection; correct.
(C) A fuel cell converts the energy of a fuel's oxidation directly into electrical energy while the reactants are fed in continuously. This is correct definition of fuel cell.
(D) The calomel electrode is a metal–insoluble salt electrode. Calomel (PbO2/Hg/KCl) is a metal electrode with an insoluble salt (PbO2) at its surface; correct.
Thus the statement NOT correct is (A).

events.stem:
Electrochemical principles govern the operation of galvanic cells and the mechanisms of corrosion.
Which one of the following statements about electrochemical cells and corrosion is correct?
(A) In rusting, oxygen is reduced at the anodic regions.
(B) In standard cell notation, the anode is written on the left.
(C) Copper blocks attached to a steel hull protect it from rusting.
(D) In a galvanic cell, the anode is the positive electrode.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Analyze each option:
(A) In rusting, oxygen is reduced at the anodic regions. In rusting (corrosion of iron), iron is oxidized (anodic) and oxygen is reduced (oxygen reduction reaction occurs at cathodic region). Thus oxygen reduction occurs at cathode, not anode. So (A) incorrect.
(B) In standard cell notation, the anode is written on the left. Standard notation: anode on left, cathode on right (oxidation left, reduction right). Actually standard notation writes anode first (oxidation) then a comma then cathode (reduction). So anode is written on the left. However some conventions write reduction half-reaction on left? Standard IUPAC: anode (oxidation) on left, cathode (reduction) on right. So (B) seems correct? Need check typical cell notation: \\text{Zn} | \\text{Zn}^{2+} || \\text{Cu}^{2+} | \\text{Cu}. Here anode is Zn (oxidation) on left, cathode Cu on right. So (B) appears correct. But statement says "In standard cell notation, the anode is written on the left." That is true. However many exam questions might consider that standard notation writes reduction on left? Let's recall: In galvanic cell notation, the anode (oxidation) is written on the left side of the cell separator, cathode on right. So (B) seems correct.
(C) Copper blocks attached to a steel hull protect it from rusting. This describes sacrificial protection (cathodic protection) where more active metal (copper is less active than iron? Actually copper is less active than iron? Standard potentials: Fe2+/Fe -0.44 V, Cu2+/Cu +0.34 V. Iron is more easily oxidized (more negative potential), so copper acts as sacrificial anode? Wait sacrificial protection uses more active metal (more negative E) that corrodes preferentially. Zinc or magnesium are used for steel. Copper is less active (more positive) than iron, so copper would not protect steel; steel would protect copper. However copper can act as cathodic protection if attached? Actually copper is less active, so it would not sacrifice; steel would corrode faster. So (C) likely incorrect.
(D) In a galvanic cell, the anode is the positive electrode. In galvanic cell, anode is negative (oxidation), cathode positive (reduction). So (D) incorrect.
Thus only (B) seems correct. However need verify if (B) is universally accepted: Some textbooks write cell notation as reduction on left? No, standard notation: anode (oxidation) left, cathode (reduction) right. So (B) correct.
Thus answer B.
members.reasoning: Need answer: correct statement? D is wrong (anode negative). C sacrificial protection true. So C correct. Return JSON.

Electrochemical principles govern the operation of galvanic devices, fuel cells, and methods of corrosion prevention.

Which one of the following statements about electrochemical cells and corrosion is NOT correct?

(A) A fuel cell converts the energy of a fuel's oxidation directly into electrical energy while the reactants are fed in continuously.
(B) In a galvanic cell, oxidation occurs at the anode, which is the negative electrode.
(C) In standard cell notation, a single vertical line represents the salt bridge.
(D) Zinc or magnesium blocks protect a steel hull because they are oxidised in preference to iron.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
Analyze each statement.
(A) Fuel cell converts fuel oxidation energy directly into electrical energy while reactants are fed continuously – correct.
(B) In a galvanic cell, oxidation occurs at the anode, which is the negative electrode – incorrect; in galvanic cells oxidation occurs at the anode which is the positive electrode (cathode is reduction).
(C) In standard cell notation, a single vertical line represents the salt bridge – correct; notation uses ||| for salt bridge.
(D) Zinc or magnesium blocks protect steel hull because they are oxidized in preference to iron – correct (cathodic protection).
Thus the statement NOT correct is (B).

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: (A) Fuel cells convert fuel oxidation energy directly to electricity with continuous reactant supply — correct. (B) In a galvanic cell, oxidation occurs at the anode, which is negative — correct. (C) In standard cell notation, a single vertical line denotes a phase boundary (e.g., electrode|electrolyte); a double vertical line (||) denotes the salt bridge — so (C) is NOT correct. (D) Zinc/magnesium are more easily oxidised than iron, acting as sacrificial anodes protecting steel — correct.
